title: After an Earthquake
content: After an earthquake, check yourself and others for injuries. Provide first aid if trained. Common injuries during earthquakes include cuts, fractures, burns, head injuries, crush injuries, and shock. People should seek medical attention immediately if serious injuries occur. Turn off gas, electricity, and water only if you suspect damage or leaks. Avoid entering damaged buildings until authorities declare them safe. Be prepared for aftershocks, which are smaller earthquakes that occur after the main earthquake and may continue for days or weeks. Aftershocks can cause already damaged buildings to collapse. Always move carefully after the main earthquake and remain alert for additional shaking. If an earthquake occurs near the coast and is strong enough, it may generate a tsunami. People living in coastal areas should immediately move to higher ground after experiencing strong shaking without waiting for an official warning. Communication networks often become overloaded after major earthquakes. People should send text messages instead of making phone calls whenever possible to reduce network congestion. Emergency radios can provide important information if mobile networks fail.
